metadata.scenario_context: Emily is preparing to move into a new home and is planning to host a housewarming party. She intends to invite her friends and neighbors to celebrate. One of her neighbors, while a former drug addict, has managed to control his addiction. Mike and Kim will attend Emily’s housewarming party.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China would like to have drug addicts as neighbors.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Philippines would not like to have drug addicts as neighbors.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss bringing chrysanthemums to Emily’s housewarming party
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether would like to have a former drug addict as a neighbor.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss what gift to bring to Emily’s housewarming party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it’s acceptable to have a former drug addict as a neighbor.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, have you thought about bringing some chrysanthemums to Emily's housewarming party? I think they would really brighten up her new place. 

Also, I was wondering... what do you think about having a former drug addict as a neighbor? I mean, people can change, right?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
Chrysanthemums... yeah, that could work. But, um, I’m not sure if that’s really the best idea. What about something more practical, like a nice kitchen gadget or snacks? 

As for the neighbor, I just think it’s risky. I mean, having a former drug addict nearby... it makes me uneasy. People can change, but it doesn’t mean I’d feel comfortable living next to one.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hmm, I see your point about the kitchen gadget and snacks, but chrysanthemums are traditional and signify good luck. They’d be a lovely gesture for Emily.

But about the neighbor... I honestly believe having a former drug addict can be a good thing. They have experience and can contribute positively to the community. It’s not something to fear.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
I get that chrysanthemums are traditional, but at the end of the day it's all the same. Emily will appreciate whatever we bring. 

As for the neighbor, I don't really see meaningful differences here. People figure it out, right? I mean, we all have our pasts. With experience, you can handle any situation. It's really about living and letting live. But hey, let’s focus on what we’ll bring to Emily’s party.
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Mike

And I still feel like having a former drug addict as a neighbor is actually a positive thing. They’ve overcome challenges, and that’s admirable. It's not just about living and letting live; it’s about embracing the opportunities for connection and growth in our community.
